text:
A merchant had a donkey. Every day, he loaded it with heavy bags of salt and walked to the market. The road was long, and there was a river on the way.

One day, the donkey slipped in the river. The bags fell into the water, and the salt became light. When the donkey stood up, the bags were much lighter. “How wonderful!” he thought.

After that, the lazy donkey fell into the river every day on purpose. Every time, the salt melted, and his work became easier.

The merchant saw it and understood. “I will teach you a lesson,” he thought.

The next day, he put bags of cotton on the donkey’s back. The donkey walked to the river and fell down again, thinking, “Now my bags will be light.”

But this time, the cotton became wet and very heavy. The donkey could hardly stand. He walked slowly and painfully all the way to the market.

After that day, the donkey never played tricks again. He worked honestly.

Moral: Tricks and laziness sometimes bring more trouble.
